### `legacy_audit.assess`

File: `legacy_audit/assess.py`

The assess stage: PostgreSQL grades, dependency security, rules, findings and effort.

It runs every scan after linking and metrics, on the linked facts and the cached per-file
results, so a changed weight, severity or disabled rule takes effect without re-analysing files.

- **class `Assessment`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `findings`, `effort`, `sbom`, `sources`, `coverage`, `target_mapping`, `unmatched_reports`
- `team_dir(loaded: LoadedConfig) -> Path | None`
- `binaries(records: list[FileRecord]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`: Compiled files (not archives), with ``has_source`` when a source file has the same stem.
- `sql_distinct(statements: list[SqlStatement]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`: One item per distinct statement text, located at its first occurrence.
- `assess(loaded: LoadedConfig, run_id: str, timestamp: str, run_dir: Path, records: list[FileRecord], entities: dict[str, list[Any]], measured: MetricsResult, hits: list[tuple[str, str, int, str]], scan_dirs: list[Path], abs_paths: dict[str, Path], cancel: threading.Event | None=None) -> Assessment`

### `legacy_audit.cli`

File: `legacy_audit/cli.py`

Command-line interface: ``legacy-audit init | scan | report | validate | facts | mcp | diff |
serve | doctor | purge-cache | version``.

- `version() -> None`: Print the tool version.
- `init(folder: Path=Path('.'), name: str | None=None, force: bool=False, copilot_layout: str='both') -> None`: Create audit.yaml, audit-overrides.yaml, audit-inputs/ and the Copilot agent files.
- `scan(config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), full: bool=False, output_dir: Path | None=None, verbose: bool=False) -> None`: Scan the configured sources and write a new run.
- `diff(run_a: str, run_b: str='latest', config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), output_dir: Path | None=None, json_out: Path | None=None, show: int=10) -> None`: Compare two runs: counts and added / removed / changed records per entity.
- `report(type_: str='tech', run: str='latest', config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), output_dir: Path | None=None, open_: bool=False, template: str | None=None) -> None`: Build reports from a run (default: the latest) into <run>/reports/.
- `validate(run: str='latest', stage: list[str] | None=None, restamp: bool=False, config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), output_dir: Path | None=None) -> None`: Check the Copilot enrichment against the scan; mark stale stages in status.json.
- `enrich(stage: list[str] | None=None, stale: bool=False, provider: str | None=None, model: str | None=None, base_url: str | None=None, check: bool=False, run: str='latest', config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), output_dir: Path | None=None) -> None`: Write the AI enrichment with any model (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Azure, Ollama).
- `facts(kind: str, filter_: list[str] | None=None, fields: str | None=None, limit: int=50, run: str='latest', config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), output_dir: Path | None=None) -> None`: Print facts of one kind as JSON (read-only; for the Copilot agent and for people).
- `mcp(config: ConfigOpt=Path('audit.yaml'), output_dir: Path | None=None) -> None`: Serve the latest run's facts to Copilot as a read-only MCP server (stdio).
- `serve(workspace: Path=Path('.'), port: int=8765, browser: bool=True, verbose: bool=False) -> None`: Start the local GUI on http://127.0.0.1:PORT (this computer only).
- `doctor(config: Path | None=None) -> None`: Check Python, Node, pptxgenjs, Mermaid CLI, Dependency-Check, OSV-Scanner, JDK and Git.
- `purge_cache_cmd(config: Path | None=None, cache_dir: Path | None=None) -> None`: Delete cloned Git sources (and, with --config, the per-file scan cache).
- internal helpers: `_setup_logging`, `_fail`, `_report_pdfs`, `_resolve`

### `legacy_audit.overrides`

File: `legacy_audit/overrides.py`

``audit-overrides.yaml``: human corrections re-applied on every run.

```yaml
files:
  exclude: ["legacy/old-copy/**"]    # dropped from all facts
  include: ["build/generated-sql/"]  # re-included despite default excludes
components:
  assign: {"src/reports/**": reports}  # move files to a (possibly new) component
  rename: {web-old: customer-portal}
  type: {customer-portal: web}
```
Each override is reported in ``run.json`` with how many items it matched; unused ones are
reported as warnings so stale overrides are noticed.

- **class `FileOverrides`**(_Strict)
  - fields: `include`, `exclude`
- **class `ComponentOverrides`**(_Strict)
  - fields: `assign`, `rename`, `type`
- **class `Overrides`**(_Strict)
  - fields: `files`, `components`
- `load_overrides(path: Path) -> Overrides`
- `apply_component_overrides(ov: Overrides, records: list[FileRecord], components: list[Component], report: dict[str, Any], warnings: list[str]) -> list[Component]`: Apply assign, rename and type overrides; update file records in place.
- internal class `_Strict`

### `legacy_audit.parallel`

File: `legacy_audit/parallel.py`

Process pool for the CPU-heavy steps (per-file analysis, PostgreSQL grading).

Results come back in input order, so a run is the same whatever the number of workers. Small
batches run in this process: starting workers costs more than it saves, and tests that patch
an analyzer keep working.

- **class `Cancelled`**(Exception)
  The user asked to stop (GUI cancel button or Ctrl+C).
- `worker_count(configured: int) -> int`: ``configured`` workers, or for 0 (auto) one per CPU less one, at most 8.
- `check(cancel: threading.Event | None) -> None`
- `ordered_map(fn: Callable[[T], R], items: Sequence[T], workers: int, *, initializer: Callable[..., None] | None=None, initargs: tuple[Any, ...]=(), cancel: threading.Event | None=None) -> Iterator[R]`: ``map(fn, items)`` across ``workers`` processes, yielding in input order.

### `legacy_audit.target`

File: `legacy_audit/target.py`

The migration target chosen in ``audit.yaml > target.profile`` (decision 161).

- ``spring-boot-angular`` (default): Java 25, Spring Boot 4, Angular 21, PostgreSQL on GCP.
- ``wildfly-gke``: the application is lifted as it is onto WildFly (Jakarta EE 11, Java 25) in
  containers on GKE; only the database moves, to PostgreSQL.
- ``none``: audit only. Nothing is suggested: no target mapping, upgrade advice beyond end of
  life and vulnerabilities, PostgreSQL grades, effort, or target and plan stages.

The scan facts and counts do not depend on the target. What does: the rule tables (each pack's
``data`` may hold a ``profiles: {<profile>: {key: value}}`` block replacing top-level keys, and
any entry may hold ``by_target: {<profile>[,<profile>...]: {field: value} | skip}``), the
``[[phrase]]`` placeholders in finding texts, the AI stages that run and the report wording.
The scan writes the choice to ``data/target.json``; the reports and the AI read it from there.

- `label(t: Target) -> str`
- `info(t: Target) -> dict[str, Any]`: What ``data/target.json`` holds.
- `read(run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]`: ``data/target.json`` of a run; a run scanned before targets existed had the default.
- `profile_of(run_dir: Path) -> str`
- `audit_only(run_dir: Path) -> bool`
- `resolve(data: dict[str, Any], profile: str) -> dict[str, Any]`: A pack's ``data`` for one target: its ``profiles`` block applied, then ``by_target``.
- `fill(text: str | None, phrases: dict[str, str]) -> str | None`: Replace ``[[name]]`` placeholders (written by analyzers and rules) with the target's wording; an unknown name becomes empty. Doubled spaces left by an empty phrase go.
- internal helpers: `_db`, `_applies`, `_resolve`

## `legacy_audit.ai`

### `legacy_audit.ai`

File: `legacy_audit/ai/__init__.py`

Optional AI enrichment with any model (``legacy-audit enrich``); the scan never uses it.


### `legacy_audit.ai.context`

File: `legacy_audit/ai/context.py`

What a model is shown for one enrichment stage, within a character budget.

Copilot in VS Code reads the facts itself, with tools. A model called over an API cannot, so
this module packs the same material into the prompt, deterministically: the agent's rules and
the stage instructions (the very files Copilot gets), the stage's JSON Schema, the scan summary,
the fact files the stage reads (``stages.py``), earlier stages it builds on and, for the
functional and component stages, the source of every batch script and program with its
comments, the code of every desktop window and ASP.NET page (their logic is in event handlers
and code-behind) and of every web service operation the application offers. Long lists are cut
with a note saying how many rows were left out, so the model knows it saw a part. Credentials
in source text are masked.

- `build(run_dir: Path, stage: Stage, budget: int, rd: RunData | None=None) -> tuple[str, str]`: (system prompt, user prompt) for ``stage`` on the run in ``run_dir``.
- `repair_prompt(answer: str, errors: list[str]) -> str`
- internal helpers: `_compact`, `_rows_block`, `_read`, `_load`, `_batch_sources`, `_numbered`, `_code_start`, `_screen_files`, `_screen_sources`, `_handler_sources`, `_stage_prompt`

### `legacy_audit.ai.providers`

File: `legacy_audit/ai/providers.py`

Model providers for ``legacy-audit enrich``: one small HTTP client per API family.

Every provider takes a system prompt and a user prompt and returns the model's text. They use
the standard library only (``urllib``), honour ``HTTPS_PROXY`` like any Python program, and never
log or store the API key: it is read from the environment variable named in the config at call
time. Families:

- ``openai``: any OpenAI-compatible ``/chat/completions`` endpoint (OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral,
  Groq, LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM, a corporate gateway...), chosen by ``base_url``;
- ``ollama``: the same API on a local Ollama (``http://localhost:11434/v1``), no key;
- ``azure-openai``: an Azure OpenAI deployment (``model`` is the deployment name);
- ``anthropic``: the Anthropic Messages API.

``copilot`` is not a client: Copilot runs inside VS Code, where the analyst picks the model.

- **class `AiError`**(Exception)
  A provider could not be called or answered with an error (message is safe to print).
- **class `Settings`** `@dataclass(frozen=True)`
  The config's ``ai`` section after environment overrides.
  - fields: `provider`, `model`, `base_url`, `api_key_env`, `api_version`, `temperature`, `max_output_tokens`, `json_mode`, `context_chars`, `timeout_seconds`, `repair_rounds`, `ca_bundle`
  - `label() -> str`
  - `url() -> str`
  - `key_env() -> str | None`
- `settings(cfg: AiConfig, **overrides: str | None) -> Settings`: Config values, then ``LEGACY_AUDIT_AI_PROVIDER`` / ``_MODEL`` / ``_BASE_URL`` / ``_API_KEY_ENV`` from the environment, then command-line overrides (when not None).
- **class `Client`**
  Calls one provider. ``transport`` is swapped in tests.
  - `__init__(s: Settings, transport: Transport | None=None) -> None`
  - `complete(system: str, user: str) -> str`
- `extract_json(text: str) -> Any`: The JSON object in a model's answer (tolerates ```json fences and text around it).
- internal helpers: `_post`, `_host`

### `legacy_audit.ai.runner`

File: `legacy_audit/ai/runner.py`

``legacy-audit enrich``: write the enrichment stages with any model, then validate them.

For each stage, in order: build the prompt (``context.py``), call the model, take the JSON out
of its answer, write ``enrichment/<stage>.json`` and run the same validator Copilot's output
goes through. When the validator finds errors, they are sent back to the model to fix
(``ai.repair_rounds`` times). A stage that still fails keeps its file, marked invalid in
``status.json``, and the run goes on; the reports show its words with a warning, as they do for
Copilot. The model only writes words: every number and id it uses is checked against the scan.

- **class `StageResult`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `stage`, `ok`, `rounds`, `errors`, `warnings`
- `pick_stages(run_dir: Path, names: list[str] | None, stale: bool) -> list[Stage]`: Stages to run, in enrichment order: the named ones, the stale and missing ones, or all.
- `run_stage(run_dir: Path, stage: Stage, client: Client, s: Settings, rd: RunData | None=None) -> StageResult`
- `enrich(run_dir: Path, s: Settings, stages: list[Stage], client: Client | None=None, progress: Callable[[str], None]=lambda _: None) -> list[StageResult]`
- `check(s: Settings, client: Client | None=None) -> str`: Send a tiny request, to test the provider, model, key and network settings.
- internal helpers: `_write`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/__init__.py`

Analyzer plugins, registered here in one place (see ``base`` for the contract).


### `legacy_audit.analyzers.autosys`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/autosys.py`

Autosys JIL (``audit-inputs/autosys/`` and any ``.jil``): ``insert_job`` / ``update_job`` /
``delete_job`` with ``job_type``, ``box_name``, ``command``, ``machine``, ``condition``,
``start_times``, ``days_of_week``, ``run_calendar``, ``date_conditions`` and ``watch_file``.

Every job is a ``BatchJob`` (scheduler ``autosys``); a ``BOX`` is a container (kind ``box``,
not counted as a job); a file watcher (``FW``) is kind ``file-watcher`` and its watched file an
inbound ``FILE`` integration. A job's command is read like a script line, so it links to the
scripts, programs, jars and Spring Batch jobs it runs. Condition predecessors become
``depends-on`` references between jobs.

- `parse_jil(text: str) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, str, str, dict[str, tuple[str, int]]]], list[int]]`: Return ([(line, verb, job, {attr: (value, line)})], unparsed line numbers).
- `predecessors(condition: str) -> list[str]`
- **class `AutosysAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.base`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/base.py`

Common analyzer interface.

An analyzer looks at one file and returns facts; it never touches the store and never looks at
other files (so its result can be cached per file). Cross-file resolution is the linker's job:
analyzers declare ``Symbol``s (what this file defines) and ``Ref``s (what it points at by name),
and the linker turns them into ``CodeEdge``s after every file is analysed.

Results are cached per file and keyed by every analyzer's ``name`` and ``version``, so bumping a
version re-analyses the files on the next run.

- **class `Symbol`**(_Model)
  Something a file defines, findable by name: a class, program, copybook, job, view...
  - fields: `kind`, `name`, `file`, `line`, `owner`, `data`
- **class `Ref`**(_Model)
  A by-name reference the linker resolves against symbols or file paths.
  - fields: `kind`, `source`, `source_label`, `target`, `target_kinds`, `file`, `line`, `report_unresolved`, `data`
- **class `Unparsed`**(_Model)
  - fields: `start`, `end`, `reason`
- **class `Coverage`**(_Model)
  - fields: `lines`, `unparsed`
  - `gap(start: int, end: int, reason: str) -> None`
- **class `Facts`** `@dataclass`
  Everything one analyzer found in one file.
  - fields: `entities`, `symbols`, `refs`, `coverage`, `units`, `windows`, `hits`
  - `add(entity: str, fact: Fact) -> Fact`
  - `symbol(kind: str, name: str, file: str, line: int | None=None, **kw: Any) -> None`
  - `ref(**kw: Any) -> None`
  - `extend(other: Facts) -> None`
  - `dump() -> dict[str, Any]`
  - `load(data: dict[str, Any]) -> Facts`
- **class `AnalyzerContext`** `@dataclass`
  What an analyzer may read: the file, its text and the configuration.
  - fields: `config`, `abs_path`, `text`, `text_rules`
  - `read_bytes() -> bytes`
- **class `Analyzer`**(Protocol)
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- `register(analyzer: Analyzer) -> Analyzer`
- `registered() -> list[Analyzer]`
- `version_key(inventory_version: str) -> str`
- internal class `_Model`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.basic`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/basic.py`

Visual Basic 6 and VB.NET, read line by line (no parser: decision 135).

Both dialects share the statement syntax this analyzer needs, so one reader serves both:

- **files**: VB6 forms (``.frm``), modules (``.bas``), classes (``.cls``), user controls
  (``.ctl``), user documents and property pages, VB6 projects (``.vbp``, ``.vbg``) and VB.NET
  source (``.vb``, ``.Designer.vb``);
- **screens**: each VB6 form and MDI form (its controls from the form header, input controls
  counted as fields, the caption as evidence), user controls and property pages as partials;
  VB.NET Windows Forms (``Inherits Form``, fields from the designer's controls) and user
  controls; ``frmX.Show``, ``Load frmX``, ``New FormX`` as navigation between screens;
- **database access**: ADO, DAO, RDO and ADO.NET calls (``Execute``, ``Open``,
  ``OpenRecordset``, ``CommandText``, ``New SqlCommand(...)``, data adapters), Dapper and Entity
  Framework raw SQL, data controls' ``RecordSource``; SQL built in code is rebuilt like the other
  languages (``&``/``+`` concatenation, ``sql = sql & ...``, ``&=``, ``StringBuilder``,
  ``String.Format``, ``IIf``; values glued in are ``?`` holes, branches make optional parts);
  stored procedures called through ``adCmdStoredProc`` / ``CommandType.StoredProcedure``;
  connection strings (credentials masked);
- **services and entry points**: VB.NET ASP.NET MVC / Web API controllers, ASMX web methods and
  WCF operations; ``Sub Main``, Windows services (``Inherits ServiceBase``), VB6 projects
  (``Type=Exe``: desktop application when it has forms, else a program);
- **dependencies**: a VB6 project's COM references and ActiveX controls as libraries
  (``source="com"``), the well-known ones also as technologies (ADO, DAO, MSXML, Crystal
  Reports, ...); every ActiveX control is a finding (it must be replaced in the target UI);
- **integrations**: URLs, connection strings, MSMQ and IBM MQ queues, Winsock hosts, files
  opened with ``Open ... For``, ``StreamReader``/``File.*``, SMTP servers;
- **tech stack**: Visual Basic 6 / VB.NET, ``Imports`` (Windows Forms, WPF, ASP.NET, WCF,
  Entity Framework, ADO.NET providers and their databases, ...).

Complexity units (``Sub``, ``Function``, ``Property``) are measured by ``metrics.units``
with the same line reader (:func:`logical_lines`).

- `strip_comment(line: str) -> str`: The code of one physical line: a ``'`` outside a string, or a leading ``REM``, starts a comment.
- `strip_comments_basic(text: str) -> str`: Comments blanked, line breaks kept (for duplication windows).
- `logical_lines(text: str, start: int=0) -> list[tuple[int, str]]`: (first line, code) per statement line: comments removed, ``_`` continuations and VB.NET implicit continuations (a line ending in ``&``, ``,``, ``(``, ``=`` or an operator) joined. ``start`` skips the first lines (a VB6 form header).
- `split_top(text: str, seps: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]`: Split ``text`` at the characters of ``seps`` outside strings and brackets: a list of (separator before, piece).
- `parse_form_header(lines: list[str]) -> tuple[_Control | None, list[_Control]]`: The form (or user control) and its controls from a VB6 designer header.
- **class `BasicAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal class `_Control`
- internal class `_Proc`
- internal class `_Class`
- internal class `_Reader` Methods: `__init__`, `run`, `_cond`, `_tracker`, `_consumed`, `_consume`, `_line`, `_proc_start`, `_end_proc`, `_blocks`, `_statement`, `_declarator`, `_assignment`, `_builder_calls`, `_calls`, `_expr_uses`, `_eval`, `_eval_parts`, `_atom`, `_format`, `_emit`, `_leftovers`, `_navigate`, `_integrations`, `_file`, `_imports`, `_vb6_form`, `_class_kind`, `_end_class`, `_proc_meaning`, `_service`
- internal helpers: `_balanced`, `_unquote`, `_args`, `_vb6_header_end`, `_com_tech`, `_vbp`, `_com`, `_route`, `_copy`, `_pop`, `_proc_body`, `_designer_fields`, `_expression_around`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.c_cpp`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/c_cpp.py`

C and C++ sources (tree-sitter-c / tree-sitter-cpp): functions, ``main()`` (a ``c-executable``
service named after the file), includes, called functions, ``system()``/``exec*``/``popen``
commands, file I/O, sockets, IBM MQ MQI calls and SQL (database client API calls and SQL text
built in buffers, see :mod:`legacy_audit.analyzers.c_sql`).

The Pro*C analyzer blanks ``EXEC SQL`` blocks and calls :func:`analyze_c` on the rest.

- `analyze_c(path: str, text: str, facts: Facts, cpp: bool=False) -> CSql`: Facts of one C/C++ text; returns the rebuilt SQL buffers for :func:`emit_c_sql`.
- `emit_c_sql(path: str, csql: CSql, facts: Facts, dialect: str | None) -> None`: SQL statements at database API call sites, then SQL-looking buffers and constants that reach the database some other way (a wrapper function).
- **class `CAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal class `_Walker` Methods: `__init__`, `run`, `_include`, `_call`, `_endpoint`, `_command`, `finish`
- internal helpers: `_str`, `_txt`, `_function_name`, `_gaps`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.c_sql`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/c_sql.py`

SQL text that C code builds in buffers, and SQL handed to database client APIs.

Buffers are followed in source order through ``strcpy``/``strncpy``/``strlcpy`` (set),
``strcat``/``strncat``/``strlcat`` (append), ``sprintf``/``snprintf`` (format; writing at
``buf + strlen(buf)`` or formatting ``"%s..."`` from the buffer itself is an append), plain
assignment of a ``char *`` and initialisers. Pro*C ``VARCHAR`` host variables (``v.arr``) are
the variable ``v``. ``#define`` string constants and file-level strings are fragments. Code
inside ``if``/loops/``switch`` is conditional, so what it adds is an optional fragment.

Pro*C looks a host variable up with :meth:`CSql.value_at` for ``PREPARE ... FROM :var`` and
``EXECUTE IMMEDIATE :var``. ODBC / DB2 CLI, OCI, libpq, MySQL and SQLite calls are SQL call
sites on their own (:attr:`CSql.calls`).

- **class `CSql`**
  Walks a C syntax tree once; see the module docstring.
  - `__init__() -> None`
  - `value_at(name: str, line: int) -> Built | None`
  - `leftovers() -> list[Built]`: Final values of buffers no SQL call site consumed (call sites behind a wrapper function) and string constants never used as a fragment.
  - `run(root: Node) -> None`
  - `eval(node: Node | None) -> Built | None`
- internal helpers: `_txt`, `_unescape`, `_line`, `_declared_name`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.cft`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/cft.py`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.cobol`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/cobol.py`

COBOL and Pro*COBOL (fixed or free format), copybooks and CICS BMS maps.

Programs: ``PROGRAM-ID`` (a ``cobol-program`` service, or a ``cics-transaction`` service when
the program runs under CICS), paragraphs, ``CALL`` (literal or a variable with a ``VALUE``),
``COPY``, ``EXEC SQL`` (dialect ``cobol.sql_dialect``; dynamic SQL rebuilt by
:mod:`legacy_audit.analyzers.cobol_sql`), ``EXEC CICS`` (``SEND/RECEIVE MAP`` to
BMS maps, ``LINK/XCTL``, ``START/RETURN TRANSID``, file commands), file ``SELECT ... ASSIGN``
and IBM MQ (MQI) calls. A program that is only ever CALLed is not counted as a service; the
linker removes it once every file is known.

BMS mapsets: every ``DFHMDI`` map is a ``Screen``; its fields are the named ``DFHMDF`` macros.

- `source_lines(text: str) -> list[str]`: Code part of each line (sequence area, indicator and identification area removed, comments blanked). Fixed format unless the source says ``>>SOURCE FORMAT FREE``.
- **class `CobolAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.cobol_sql`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/cobol_sql.py`

SQL text that COBOL builds in working storage for ``PREPARE ... FROM :var`` and
``EXECUTE IMMEDIATE :var``.

Values come from ``VALUE`` clauses, then the procedure division in source order: ``MOVE x TO
a b`` (sets; a reference-modified target ``A(P:N)`` is an append), ``STRING ... INTO a`` (sets,
or appends when ``a`` is its first operand or ``WITH POINTER`` is used) and ``INITIALIZE``.
Statements inside ``IF``/``EVALUATE``/inline ``PERFORM`` are conditional (a period ends them
all). A DB2 varying-length host variable (a group with a level-49 length and a level-49 text
item) is looked up through its text item. Operands that are not known become ``?`` holes.

- **class `CobolSql`**
  Walks the code area of a program once; see the module docstring.
  - `__init__() -> None`
  - `value_at(name: str, line: int) -> Built | None`
  - `run(lines: list[str]) -> None`: ``lines``: the code area, one entry per source line, ``EXEC`` blocks blanked.
- internal helpers: `_literal`, `_name`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.csharp`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/csharp.py`

C# (tree-sitter-c-sharp): Windows Forms, WPF, ASP.NET, WCF, Windows services and data
access (decision 136).

One parse per file finds:

- **screens**: Windows Forms forms (``: Form``; fields from the designer's controls) and user
  controls (partials); WPF windows come from their ``.xaml`` (``dotnet`` analyzer), the code
  behind only adds navigation; ``new X().Show()``/``ShowDialog()`` and ``var f = new X();
  f.Show()`` are navigation between screens;
- **services**: ASP.NET MVC actions (``: Controller``), Web API actions (``: ApiController``,
  ``: ControllerBase``, ``[ApiController]``) with their ``[Route]``/``[HttpGet(...)]`` paths,
  ASMX ``[WebMethod]`` and WCF ``[OperationContract]`` operations;
- **entry points and jobs**: ``static Main`` (a desktop application when it runs
  ``Application.Run``/``ShowDialog``/a WPF ``App``, else a program, which makes its component
  batch work), Windows services (``: ServiceBase``) and hosted services
  (``: BackgroundService``), Hangfire ``RecurringJob.AddOrUpdate`` and Quartz.NET cron triggers
  as batch jobs;
- **database access**: ADO.NET commands and adapters (``new SqlCommand(sql, cn)``,
  ``CommandText = ...``), Dapper (``Query``, ``Execute``, ...), Entity Framework raw SQL
  (``FromSqlRaw``, ``SqlQuery``, ``ExecuteSqlRaw``, ...), Entity Framework LINQ on a
  ``DbSet`` (kept as readable ORM text, not parsed), entity-to-table mappings (``[Table]``,
  ``DbSet<T>``); SQL built in code is rebuilt (``+``, ``+=``, ``$"..."`` interpolation,
  ``StringBuilder``, ``string.Format``, ``?:``), the run-time pieces being ``?`` holes;
  stored procedures through ``CommandType.StoredProcedure``; connection strings (masked);
- **integrations**: URLs, connection strings, MSMQ queues, SMTP servers, files read or written
  (``File.*``, ``StreamReader``/``StreamWriter``/``FileStream``);
- **tech stack**: C#, the ``using`` namespaces (Windows Forms, WPF, ASP.NET, WCF, Entity
  Framework, ADO.NET providers and their databases, Quartz.NET, Hangfire, MSMQ, ...).

- **class `CSharpAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `__init__() -> None`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal class `_Class`
- internal class `_Method`
- internal class `_Visitor` Methods: `__init__`, `run`, `_decls`, `_using`, `_class`, `_field`, `_property`, `_method_decl`, `_body`, `_end_method`, `_service_for`, `_cond`, `_tracker`, `_consumed`, `_consume`, `_walk`, `_value_node`, `_declarator`, `_walk_value`, `_assignment`, `_eval_without_head`, `_invocation`, `_creation`, `_uses`, `_literal`, `_eval`, `_format`, `_emit`, `_orm`, `_leftovers`, `_service`, `_entry`, `_navigate`, `_file`, `_hangfire`, `_quartz`, `_job`
- internal helpers: `_txt`, `_line`, `_string`, `_args`, `_named_arg`, `_callee`, `_type_name`, `_attributes`, `_cron_text`, `_iter`, `_copy`, `_designer_fields`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.deps`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/deps.py`

Undeclared dependencies: jars/wars/ears (manifest, pom.properties, file name), npm
``package.json`` (with the Node.js version it asks for), npm lock files (``package-lock.json``,
``npm-shrinkwrap.json``, ``yarn.lock``, ``pnpm-lock.yaml``: the exact version of every package,
direct or not), Bower ``bower.json`` and bundled JavaScript libraries.

Lock-file entries are ``source="npm-lock"``; the linker folds a ``package.json`` entry into the
lock file's exact version when both sit in one folder (``merge_npm_versions``). Packages only
the lock file lists are kept as ``declared=False``, ``scope="transitive"``, so a vulnerability
OSV-Scanner reports on one of them matches a library (decision 129).

- `npm_version(spec: str) -> str | None`: The version a ``package.json`` range starts from (``^17.3.0`` -> ``17.3.0``); None for tags, URLs, paths and ``*``.
- `node_version(spec: str) -> str | None`: Major.minor of a Node.js engines range or ``.nvmrc`` (``>=18.17`` -> ``18.17``).
- `jar_identity(name: str, data: bytes) -> tuple[str | None, str, str | None]`: (group, artifact, version) from pom.properties, the manifest, then the file name.
- **class `DepsAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal helpers: `_manifest`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.dotnet`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/dotnet.py`

Microsoft .NET and Windows desktop files that are not code: project files, NuGet package
lists, configuration, window layouts and ASP.NET pages (decision 134).

- **projects** (``.csproj``, ``.vbproj``, ``Directory.Build.props``): the language (C# or
  VB.NET, with ``LangVersion``), the runtime (.NET Framework 2.0 to 4.8.1, .NET Core, .NET 5+,
  .NET Standard), the application kind (``OutputType`` ``WinExe`` = desktop application,
  Windows Forms / WPF / ASP.NET / Worker service from the SDK, properties and references),
  NuGet ``PackageReference`` libraries, ``..\packages\<id>.<version>`` hint paths and
  project-to-project references;
- **NuGet lists**: ``packages.config``, ``Directory.Packages.props`` (central versions) and
  ``packages.lock.json`` (exact versions, direct and transitive);
- **solutions** (``.sln``): the Visual Studio version;
- **configuration** (``app.config``, ``web.config``, ``*.exe.config``, ``appsettings*.json``):
  connection strings as database integrations (credentials masked, a password is a finding)
  and WCF client endpoints as SOAP integrations;
- **layouts**: WPF / WinUI ``.xaml`` windows, pages and user controls and JavaFX ``.fxml``
  views as screens; the WPF ``App.xaml`` start-up window as an entry point;
- **ASP.NET pages**: Web Forms ``.aspx`` (``.ascx`` controls and ``.master`` pages are
  partials) with their ``SqlDataSource`` SQL, Razor ``.cshtml``/``.vbhtml`` views and Blazor
  ``.razor`` components as screens;
- **Windows Task Scheduler**: exported task definitions (``.xml``) and ``schtasks /create`` in
  batch and PowerShell scripts as batch jobs (scheduler ``windows-task``).

The code itself is read by the ``csharp`` and ``basic`` (VB6, VB.NET) analyzers; the helpers
for connection strings and ADO.NET providers below are shared with them.

- `connection_string(text: str) -> tuple[str | None, str, bool] | None`: (database product, target, has a password) of an ADO / ADO.NET / ODBC connection string, or None when the text is not one. The target never carries credentials.
- `add_connection(facts: Facts, text: str, path: str, line: int | None, protocol: str, provider: str='') -> bool`: A connection string found in code or configuration: a DB integration, the database as a technology and, when it holds a password, a credential finding. True when it was one.
- `framework_version(tfm: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None`: (runtime, version) of a target framework moniker or ``TargetFrameworkVersion``: ``net48``/``v4.8`` -> .NET Framework 4.8, ``netcoreapp3.1`` -> .NET Core 3.1, ``net8.0-windows`` -> .NET 8.0, ``netstandard2.0`` -> .NET Standard 2.0.
- **class `DotnetAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal helpers: `_xml_line`, `_parse`, `_project`, `_nuget_version`, `_nuget`, `_packages_config`, `_nuget_lock`, `_solution`, `_config`, `_appsettings`, `_layout`, `_aspx`, `_razor`, `_task_xml`, `_schtasks`, `_program`, `_task`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.dynsql`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/dynsql.py`

Rebuilding SQL text that code assembles at run time, shared by the C/Pro*C and COBOL
analyzers (the Java analyzer keeps its own tree-based version with the same fields).

A ``Built`` value is the text a variable holds at some point: every fragment (``text``), only
the fragments added on every code path (``minimal``), the run-time pieces shown as ``?`` and
classified by :func:`hole_kind` (``value`` or ``structural``), and whole alternative texts
(``variants``) from ternaries and branch-only reassignments. ``Tracker`` keeps each variable's
history in source order so a ``PREPARE ... FROM :var`` or an API call can look up the value
the variable had on that line.

- **class `Built`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `text`, `line`, `minimal`, `value_holes`, `structural_holes`, `fragments`, `optional`, `how`, `lines`, `variants`
  - `base() -> str`
  - `dynamic() -> bool`
- `lit(text: str, line: int) -> Built`
- `empty(line: int) -> Built`
- `hole(before: str, line: int) -> Built`
- `concat(a: Built, b: Built, optional: bool=False) -> Built`
- `join(parts: list[Built], line: int) -> Built`
- `choice(a: Built, b: Built) -> Built`: ``cond ? a : b``: the text of ``a``, with ``b`` as a variant.
- `update(prev: Built | None, new: Built, cond: bool, append: bool) -> Built`: The value of a variable after an assignment (``append`` = added to the end); ``cond`` when the statement runs on some code paths only.
- `format_c(fmt: Built, args: list[Built | None], line: int, before: str='') -> Built`: ``sprintf`` text: each conversion takes the next argument (its rebuilt text, or a hole). ``before`` is the text already in the buffer when the result is appended to it.
- **class `Tracker`**
  Values of text variables in source order; ``at`` answers "what did it hold here".
  - `__init__() -> None`
  - `get(name: str) -> Built | None`
  - `assign(name: str, new: Built, line: int, cond: bool, append: bool) -> None`
  - `at(name: str, line: int) -> Built | None`: The value just before ``line``; a variable only built further down the source (a paragraph or function that runs earlier) gives its last value.
- **class `Rebuilt`**(Protocol)
  - fields: `fragments`, `optional`, `value_holes`, `structural_holes`, `how`, `lines`, `variants`
  - `base() -> str`
- `fill(fact: SqlStatement, built: Rebuilt) -> SqlStatement`: Copy how the text was rebuilt onto the statement, with evidence for each fragment.

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.embedded`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/embedded.py`

Embedded SQL (``EXEC SQL ... ;`` in Pro*C, ``EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC`` in COBOL / Pro*COBOL).

Each block becomes a ``SqlStatement`` with source ``embedded``; cursor declarations count as the
SELECT they declare; ``OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE``, ``WHENEVER``, ``CONNECT`` and transaction control are
not statements. ``PREPARE``/``EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`` from a host variable are rebuilt from the code
that fills the variable when the caller can (see ``resolve``), else recorded as ``DYNAMIC``.
Callers get the block spans back so they can blank them before parsing the host language.

- **class `EmbeddedResult`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `statements`, `includes`, `spans`, `unparsed`
- `extract(text: str, *, file: str, dialect: str | None, cobol: bool, resolve: Callable[[str, int], Built | None] | None=None) -> EmbeddedResult`: EXEC SQL blocks of C (``;``) or COBOL (``END-EXEC``) text. COBOL callers pass the code area only (see ``cobol.source_lines``), so sequence and identification columns are gone. ``resolve(":host-var", line)`` rebuilds the text a dynamic statement prepares.
- `block_spans(text: str, *, cobol: bool) -> list[tuple[int, int]]`: Character spans of the ``EXEC SQL`` blocks (the same spans :func:`extract` returns).
- `blank_spans(text: str, spans: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> str`: Replace each span with spaces, keeping newlines so line numbers stay right.

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.integrations`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/integrations.py`

Building ``Integration`` facts. Each usage is recorded per (type, target, direction); MQ/JMS
queues per queue, their direction derived from producers and consumers when everything is
merged. The merge then keeps one integration per interface (``consolidation_key``).

- `integration(*, type: str, target: str, direction: str, file: str, line: int | None, role: str | None=None, protocol: str | None=None, details: dict[str, str] | None=None) -> Integration`: One usage of an integration. ``role`` is 'producer' or 'consumer' (queues).
- `mask_userinfo(url: str) -> str`: Drop user:password@ from a URL and user/password@ from an Oracle thin URL.
- `parse_jdbc(url: str) -> tuple[str, str]`: (database product, target) for a JDBC URL; target has no credentials.
- `classify_url(url: str, soap_hint: bool=False) -> tuple[str, str] | None`: (type, target) for a URL found in code or config; None for spec/namespace URLs.
- `consolidation_key(type: str, target: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]`: (family, key, display target): integrations with the same family and key are one interface, whatever direction, spelling or default port each usage was written with.
- `merge_directions(directions: set[str]) -> str`: inbound + outbound is both; a concrete direction wins over defined and unknown.
- `identity_provider(it: Integration) -> str | None`: The identity provider an integration calls (Okta, Entra ID, ...), or None.
- `describe(it: Integration) -> tuple[str, str]`: (purpose, one-sentence description) of a consolidated integration, from its facts only; a row of one external service also says what it groups (endpoints, queues, files).
- internal helpers: `_host_port`, `_host_and_path`, `_listed`, `_grouped`, `_describe`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.servers`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/servers.py`

Application servers and web servers: which ones the application is built for or runs on.

Read from the files that only make sense on one product (decision 131):

- deployment descriptors in the code: ``weblogic.xml`` and the other ``weblogic-*.xml``,
  ``ibm-web-bnd``/``ibm-web-ext`` and the other ``ibm-*`` bindings (``.xml`` or the older
  ``.xmi``), ``jboss-web.xml`` and the other ``jboss-*.xml``, ``*-ds.xml``, Tomcat's
  ``context.xml``, GlassFish/Payara, Jetty, Resin and OC4J descriptors;
- server configuration (in the code or in ``audit-inputs/server-config/``): WebLogic
  ``config.xml``, JBoss/WildFly ``standalone.xml``/``domain.xml``, Tomcat ``server.xml`` and
  ``catalina.properties``, WebSphere Liberty ``server.xml``, Apache HTTP Server / IBM HTTP Server
  / Oracle HTTP Server ``httpd.conf`` (and their WebLogic / WebSphere plug-ins, ``mod_jk``),
  Nginx ``nginx.conf``, IIS ``web.config``;
- container images (``Dockerfile``: ``FROM tomcat:9.0``, ``FROM nginx:1.25``, ``FROM node:18``);
- start and admin scripts (``startWebLogic.sh``, ``wsadmin``, ``catalina.sh``, ``standalone.sh``,
  ``asadmin``, ``apachectl``);
- vendor APIs imported by Java code (``weblogic.*``, ``com.ibm.websphere.*``, ``org.jboss.ejb3``).

Each is a tech-stack item (category ``app-server`` or ``web-server``, ``runtime`` for Node.js and
Java images) with the file and line as evidence, and a version only when the file states one
(``<domain-version>``, a DTD naming the release, an image tag). Server-specific descriptors and
vendor APIs are also ``server-specific`` findings. What becomes of them depends on the target
(``audit.yaml > target.profile``), so their texts carry ``[[server-move]]``,
``[[server-api]]`` and ``[[server-remediation]]``, filled in by the assess stage
(``rules/target-mapping.yaml > phrases``).

- **class `ServersAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal class `_Found` Methods: `__init__`, `add`, `finding`, `config_finding`
- internal helpers: `_version_tag`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.typescript`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/typescript.py`

TypeScript and JavaScript (tree-sitter-typescript): Angular, AngularJS and Node.js code.

One parse per file finds:

- **Angular** (2+): components (``@Component``) with their template and selector, the router
  (``Routes`` arrays, lazy ``loadComponent``), the bootstrap component, ``HttpClient`` calls;
- **AngularJS** (1.x): modules, controllers, components, ``$routeProvider``/``$stateProvider``
  routes and their templates, ``$http``/``$resource`` calls;
- **Node.js services**: Express/Koa/Fastify/hapi routes and NestJS controllers as services, the
  server start-up as an entry point, ``app.use('/prefix', router)`` mounts (applied by the
  linker), outgoing calls (``fetch``, ``axios``, ...);
- **database access**: SQL in strings and template literals (rebuilt like the Java analyzer:
  ``+``, ``+=`` and ``${...}`` pieces become holes), TypeORM, Prisma, Sequelize and Knex calls as
  ORM statements on their entity (the SQL is generated at run time), entity-to-table mappings,
  database connection settings;
- **scheduled jobs**: ``node-cron``, ``cron``, ``node-schedule``, Agenda and NestJS
  ``@Cron``/``@Interval``/``@Timeout`` as batch jobs (scheduler ``node-cron``);
- URLs in strings as integrations (HTTP, SOAP, FTP, database and AMQP connection strings).

Prisma schemas (``schema.prisma``) are read here too: their models map entities to tables.

Templates (``.html``) are read by the ``web`` analyzer, which marks Angular and AngularJS ones;
a component points at its template with a ``renders`` reference and routes point at components
with ``forwards`` references, so the linker can tell routed screens from sub-components
(decision 130).

- `url_path(text: str) -> str | None`: The path part of a URL built in code, for matching an API route: holes (``?``) before the first ``/`` are the base URL; ``http://host/x`` -> ``/x``. None for absolute URLs to another system (they are integrations) and for text that is not a path.
- **class `TypeScriptAnalyzer`**
  - fields: `name`, `version`
  - `__init__() -> None`
  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`
  - `analyze(file: FileRecord, ctx: AnalyzerContext) -> Facts`
- internal class `_Scope`: String values known in a function body: variables and their rebuilt text.
- internal class `_Visitor` Methods: `__init__`, `run`, `_imports`, `_constants`, `_repo_binding`, `_eval`, `_is_string_expr`, `_walk`, `_mark`, `_declaration`, `_assignment`, `_leftovers`, `_text_found`, `_urls`, `_orm`, `_service`, `_entry`, `_job`, `_api_call`, `_call`, `_route`, `_route_service`, `_new`, `_object`, `_db_config`, `_orm_call`, `_schedule_call`, `_job_name`, `_class`, `_angular_component`, `_bootstraps`, `_nest_routes`, `_member_decorators`, `_angularjs`, `_angularjs_route`, `_file_level`

### `legacy_audit.analyzers.websvc`

File: `legacy_audit/analyzers/websvc.py`

Web services (REST and SOAP): the shared builders analyzers use, and the analyzer for the XML
files that describe or deploy web services.

Services the application **offers** are ``Service`` facts (``rest-operation``,
``soap-operation``, routes) found by the language analyzers; the XML deployment files add the
ones written only in configuration (Apache Axis ``*.wsdd``, Axis2 ``services.xml``). Services it
**calls** are ``web_services`` facts with ``side: called``, one per call site; WSDL files are
``side: contract`` until the linker knows whether the application offers or calls the service
they describe. The linker (``linker/websvc.py``) folds all of them into one row per web service
(decision 133).

This analyzer reads:

- WSDL 1.1 and 2.0 files: service, ports and their address, port type operations, namespace;
- Apache Axis 1 deployment descriptors (``server-config.wsdd``, ``deploy.wsdd``);
- Apache Axis2 ``services.xml``;
- JAX-WS RI ``sun-jaxws.xml`` and Apache CXF ``jaxws:``/``jaxrs:`` Spring XML (where each
  implementation class is published, and CXF clients);
- ``web.xml`` servlets of web service frameworks (Axis, Axis2, CXF, Jersey, RESTEasy, JAX-WS RI,
  Spring-WS) and the URL they are mapped to.

- `split_url(text: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]`: (``scheme://host[:port]`` or None, path) of a URL found in code. The base is None when the text is a path, or when the host is built at run time (``?``) or is a placeholder.
- `operation(name: str, *, method: str | None=None, path: str | None=None, handler: str | None=None, file: str | None=None, line: int | None=None) -> WebOperation`
- `rest_op_name(method: str | None, path: str | None) -> str`
- `called(*, style: str, name: str, framework: str, file: str, line: int | None, url: str | None=None, op: str | None=None, method: str | None=None, handler: str | None=None, wsdl: str | None=None, namespace: str | None=None) -> WebService`: One call site of another system's web service. ``url`` is the address as written (an absolute URL, a path or a ``?`` hole); ``op`` the SOAP operation, when known.
- `offered_service(facts: Facts, *, name: str, kind: str, file: str, line: int | None, handler: str, url: str | None, protocol: str, framework: str, web_service: str | None) -> None`: A web service operation the application offers, as a ``Service`` fact.

  - `supports(file: FileRecord) -> bool`

### `legacy_audit.copilot.install`

File: `legacy_audit/copilot/install.py`

Install the Copilot agent, instructions, prompt files and schemas into a legacy workspace.

``legacy-audit init`` calls ``install``. Copilot's file names changed across releases (custom
chat modes became custom agents), so the agent is written as ``.github/agents/*.agent.md``,
``.github/chatmodes/*.chatmode.md`` or both. Front-matter is kept to ``description`` and
``tools`` so format changes stay cheap. Every value is quoted: a plain YAML value holding
": " is invalid, and current VS Code builds then drop the agent or prompt file (decision 173).

User edits are kept: ``.github/legacy-audit/installed.json`` records the hash of each file as
installed. On a later ``init``, a file still equal to that hash is updated in place; a file the
user changed is left alone and the new version is written next to it as ``<name>.new``.

- **class `Installed`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `path`, `action`
- `assets(layout: str, model: str | None=None) -> dict[str, str]`: Relative path -> content for a layout; ``model`` pins the agent's chat model.
- `install(folder: Path, layout: str='both', model: str | None=None) -> list[Installed]`
- internal helpers: `_asset`, `_q`, `_sha`

## `legacy_audit.enrich`

### `legacy_audit.enrich`

File: `legacy_audit/enrich/__init__.py`


### `legacy_audit.enrich.models`

File: `legacy_audit/enrich/models.py`

Enrichment files the Copilot agent writes, one pydantic model per stage.

The agent interprets; it never counts. So every enrichment file follows three conventions that
``legacy-audit validate`` checks:

- **Figures** (``{metric, value, estimate}``) carry every number. ``metric`` is a path into
  ``audit-summary.json`` (``counts.services.total``) or ``effort.json`` (``effort.likely``); the
  value must equal the scan's unless ``estimate: true``.
- **Claims** (risks, flows, classifications...) cite ``evidence: [{file, line}]`` or say
  ``assumption: true``.
- **References** to facts use their ids in fields ending ``_id`` / ``_ids``, and component names
  in ``component`` / ``components``; both must exist in the run.

``meta.built_from`` is stamped by ``legacy-audit validate`` (the agent leaves it out); it records
the hash of every fact file and upstream stage the stage was built from, which is how a later
re-scan knows the stage is stale.

### `legacy_audit.enrich.stages`

File: `legacy_audit/enrich/stages.py`

Enrichment stages (thirteen; stage 8 writes two files) and what each is built from.

``inputs`` are fact files in ``data/`` (an entity name, ``effort``, ``target-mapping`` or
``target``; the stages that suggest something read ``target``, so changing the target makes
them stale);
``after`` are earlier stages whose output the stage reads. A stage is stale when the hash of one
of them changed since it was built (see ``status.py``). Keep ``inputs`` to what the stage really
reads: adding Autosys JIL changes services, batch jobs and the tech stack, so flows, risks, plan
and narratives go stale, but classification (components and entry points only) does not.

- **class `Stage`** `@dataclass(frozen=True)`
  - fields: `number`, `name`, `title`, `model`, `inputs`, `after`
  - `file() -> str`
- `fact_file(kind: str) -> str`

### `legacy_audit.enrich.status`

File: `legacy_audit/enrich/status.py`

Enrichment staleness, stamping and carry-over between runs.

Each stage file records in ``meta.built_from`` the hash of every fact file and upstream stage it
was built from (stamped by ``legacy-audit validate``). After a re-scan the new run's hashes are
compared with those: a stage whose inputs changed, or whose upstream stage is stale, is stale.
``enrichment/status.json`` lists the result and ``/audit-enrich stale`` re-runs those stages.

Where ``latest`` is a copy rather than a symlink (Windows without developer mode), the agent writes
into ``latest/enrichment/``; ``sync_from_latest`` brings those files into the run folder first so
nothing written there is lost.

- `enrichment_dir(run_dir: Path) -> Path`
- `stage_hash(path: Path) -> str`: Hash of a stage file's content without its ``meta`` (so stamping does not change it).
- `active_stages(run_dir: Path) -> list[Stage]`: The stages this run's target needs: all of them, or without the target stages when there is no target (audit only, ``data/target.json``).
- `current_hashes(run_dir: Path, stage: Stage) -> dict[str, str]`
- `stamp(run_dir: Path, stage: Stage, *, force: bool=False) -> bool`: Record what the stage was built from, when it is not recorded yet (or ``force``).
- `compute_status(run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]`: Present / stale per stage; written to ``enrichment/status.json``.
- `write_status(run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]`
- `latest_copy(run_dir: Path) -> Path | None`: ``<output>/latest`` when it is a plain copy of this run, else None.
- `sync_from_latest(run_dir: Path) -> None`: Bring files the agent wrote into a copied ``latest/enrichment`` into the run folder.
- `sync_to_latest(run_dir: Path) -> None`: After stamping, put the run's enrichment back into a copied ``latest``.
- `carry_over(previous_run: Path | None, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any] | None`: Copy the previous run's enrichment into a new run and mark what is now stale.
- internal helpers: `_sha`, `_read`, `_changed`

### `legacy_audit.enrich.validate`

File: `legacy_audit/enrich/validate.py`

``legacy-audit validate``: check the agent's enrichment against the scan.

Per stage file, in order:

1. JSON Schema (the pydantic model): shape, enums, and every claim citing evidence or saying
   ``assumption: true``.
2. References: ids in ``*_id`` / ``*_ids`` fields exist in the facts; component names exist.
3. Numbers come from facts: every figure's value equals the scan's value at its ``metric`` path,
   unless marked ``estimate: true``. Counts written in prose ("12 services") that differ from the
   scan are reported as warnings, since prose may talk about a subset.
4. Evidence: each cited file exists in the scanned source and the line is inside it.

A stage with no errors gets ``meta.built_from`` stamped (the hashes it was built from), then
``enrichment/status.json`` is rewritten.

- **class `Message`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `level`, `stage`, `where`, `text`
- **class `Report`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `run_dir`, `messages`, `checked`, `stamped`, `status`
  - `errors() -> list[Message]`
  - `warnings() -> list[Message]`
  - `ok() -> bool`
- `lookup(facts: dict[str, Any], metric: str) -> Any`
- `validate_run(run_dir: Path, stages: list[str] | None=None, restamp: bool=False) -> Report`: Validate the enrichment of one run; stamp the stages that pass; rewrite status.json.
- internal class `_Checker` Methods: `__init__`, `check`, `_references`, `_figures`, `_lines`, `_evidence`, `_target`, `_prose`
- internal helpers: `_walk`, `_dicts`, `_same`

### `legacy_audit.inventory.components`

File: `legacy_audit/inventory/components.py`

Default component detection from build files and folder layout.

Rules, per source root:
1. Every folder holding a build or project file (pom.xml, build.xml, build.gradle, Makefile,
   an Eclipse .project, CMakeLists.txt, a Visual Studio project, package.json, angular.json,
   bower.json, ...) is a component root.
2. If the source root itself has no build file, the folder layout decides (decision 114):
   - folders named like the *parts* of an application (src, WebContent, conf, properties,
     scripts, ksh, sql, jcl, ...) are never components on their own while they sit next to
     code: an application folder with ``src/`` and ``WebContent/`` is one component holding
     its Java, its JSPs, its scripts and its properties;
   - a folder holding an application's code folders (src, java, WebContent, WebRoot, webapp,
     ...) is one component; application folders nested in it become components of their own;
   - a folder holding only other application folders (no files of its own, no part folders)
     is a container, not a component: each folder under it is looked at the same way;
   - at a root that is not itself an application, every top-level folder is a component,
     including part folders (a shared ``config/`` becomes a config component); loose files go
     to a component named after the root.
3. Maven and Gradle decide when they are there (decision 166): a ``pom.xml`` with
   ``<packaging>pom</packaging>`` (a parent or aggregator) and a Gradle root with
   ``settings.gradle`` are *groups*, not components; each module they list is a component. What
   sits beside the modules in a group folder (``scripts/``, ``config/``, ``sql/``) follows rule
   2, so a shared ``config/`` is a config component; leftovers with no code, script, SQL or
   configuration (the parent pom itself, a README) belong to no component.
4. A batch folder (``batch``, ``batches``, ``jobs``, ``cron``, ...) holding two or more batch
   folders is split: each is a batch component, and what they share (``common/``, ``lib/``,
   ``config/``, loose files) is one component of its own (decision 167).
5. Components listed in ``audit.yaml`` take precedence over 1 to 4 for the files under them.
A file belongs to the deepest component root above it.

Then the components are grouped (``inventory.component_grouping: auto``, decision 176; see
``legacy_audit.inventory.grouping``): a Maven / Gradle library module goes into the one
deployable (war, ear, runnable or batch jar) that uses it, the folders beside the modules of a
group are one component, and without a build file part folders of the same technology (COBOL
and BMS, JCL and PROCLIB, the batches of one batch folder) are one component.

- `is_project_file(name: str) -> bool`
- **class `Candidate`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `root`, `path`, `detected_by`, `name`, `type`, `build_files`, `artifact`, `packaging`, `in_group`, `app`, `batch_kid`, `level`, `parts`, `jvm_module`, `deps`, `runnable`
- **class `BuildInfo`** `@dataclass`
  What a folder's ``pom.xml`` or ``settings.gradle`` says about its modules.
  - fields: `artifact`, `packaging`, `modules`, `gradle_root`, `deps`, `runnable`
- `read_pom(base: str, text: str) -> BuildInfo`: artifactId, packaging and modules (``<modules>`` and those of every profile).
- `read_gradle_build(base: str, text: str) -> BuildInfo`: Projects a module's ``build.gradle`` depends on (``implementation project(':core')``), as folders relative to the source root, and whether it builds an application.
- `read_gradle_settings(base: str, text: str) -> BuildInfo`: Projects a ``settings.gradle`` includes (``include 'core', ':batch:billing'``).
- `in_batch_folder(path: str) -> bool`
- `in_shared_folder(path: str) -> bool`: A file of the shared part of a batch folder (``batch/common/functions.ksh``): a helper of the batches, not batch work of its own.
- `infer_type(files: list[FileRecord], name: str='') -> ComponentType`: The type from the inventory alone; the linker refines it from what was found (services, screens, jobs). Mixed components take the type of their most specific part: Java + JSP is web; Java or C + ksh + properties is batch when a script or folder says so.
- `composition(files: list[FileRecord]) -> dict[str, int]`
- `detect_components(records: list[FileRecord], root_names: list[str], specs: list[ComponentSpec], read: ReadText | None=None, grouping: str='auto') -> tuple[list[Component], dict[str, str]]`: Return components and a map file id -> component name. ``read`` gives the text of a build file (pom.xml, settings.gradle, build.gradle) so Maven and Gradle can say which folders are modules, which are parents and which modules use which; without it the folder layout decides. ``grouping`` is ``auto`` (group them, decision 176) or ``module`` (one per module and folder).
- `disk_reader(roots: dict[str, Path], max_bytes: int=2000000) -> ReadText`: A ``ReadText`` over source roots on disk (build files only; never written to).
- internal helpers: `_module_dir`, `_runnable`, `_parent`, `_under`, `_rel_in_root`, `_desktop`, `_layout_candidates`, `_build_info`, `_gradle_builds`, `_groups`, `_shared_type`

### `legacy_audit.inventory.grouping`

File: `legacy_audit/inventory/grouping.py`

Group the components found by the folder and build-file rules (decision 176).

``inventory.component_grouping: auto`` (the default) runs two steps on the candidates of
``legacy_audit.inventory.components``; ``module`` keeps one component per module and folder.

1. Maven / Gradle (the pom decides): every module that runs on its own is a *deployable* (a
   ``war``, ``ear``, ``rar`` or ``sar``, a Spring Boot or other runnable jar, a module whose files
   make it web, batch, desktop, front end or API). A library module (a plain ``jar`` or ``ejb``)
   goes into the deployable that uses it, read from the ``<dependencies>`` of the poms
   (``project(':core')`` in a ``build.gradle``), directly or through other libraries. A library
   used by several deployables, or by none, stays a component of its own.
2. Part folders (technology decides): in a Maven / Gradle group folder, the folders beside the
   modules (``config/``, ``scripts/``, ``ops/batch/...``) are one component
   ``<group>-scripts-config``. Without a build file, part folders found side by side are grouped
   by technology: COBOL and BMS (with their copybooks) are ``cobol-online``, JCL and PROCLIB
   ``jcl-jobs``, SQL folders ``database``, the batches of one batch folder and what they share
   one component named after the batch folder, configuration and utility scripts
   ``shared-scripts-config``. Configuration and scripts beside exactly one application go into it.

Each grouped component lists the folders it is made of in ``parts``. The batch count does not
change: it is one batch per entry point whatever component holds it (decision 168).

- `group_candidates(candidates: list[Candidate], members: Members, group_names: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> list[Candidate]`: The candidates after grouping; ``members`` is updated for the new and grown ones.
- internal helpers: `_deployable`, `_fold_libraries`, `_family`, `_has_tech`, `_parent`, `_common`, `_is_part`, `_name`, `_group_parts`

- `extended_path(path: Path | str, windows: bool=sys.platform == 'win32') -> str`: On Windows, the ``\\?\`` form of an absolute path, which is not limited to 260 characters (legacy trees nest deeply). Elsewhere the path unchanged.
- `is_minified(path: Path, name: str) -> bool`: A minified or bundled JavaScript/CSS file, by its name (``app.min.js``, ``main.3f2a9c1b.js``, ``vendor.bundle.js``, source maps) or its content (a line over 2,000 characters in the first 64 KB, and few lines).
- `build_output_files(folder: Path) -> int`: Number of files in ``folder`` when it looks like compiler or IDE output (compiled files and no source or script), else 0.
- `eclipse_output_dirs(folder: Path) -> list[str]`: Output folders declared in an Eclipse ``.classpath`` (``kind="output"``), relative to ``folder``.
- `walk(root_name: str, root: Path, filters: Filters, subpaths: list[str] | None=None, skipped: list[SkippedPath] | None=None) -> Iterator[WalkedFile]`: Yield selected files in a stable (sorted) order. Symlinked folders and files are not followed (no loops, nothing outside the tree); on Windows paths over 260 characters work.
- internal helpers: `_is_compiled`, `_nuget_packages`

### `legacy_audit.inventory.worker`

File: `legacy_audit/inventory/worker.py`

Inventory and analysis of one file: the unit of work the scan runs in parallel.

``setup`` is called once per worker process with what every file needs; ``process`` reads one
file and returns what goes into the file cache. Nothing here touches the store or the cache, so
the result is the same in a worker as in the main process.

## `legacy_audit.linker`

### `legacy_audit.linker`

File: `legacy_audit/linker/__init__.py`

Cross-file linking and classification (runs on every scan, after all files are analysed).


### `legacy_audit.linker.aggregate`

File: `legacy_audit/linker/aggregate.py`

Merging per-file facts into one fact set: the same integration, library, tech item, batch job
or database object found in several files becomes one fact with all its evidence.

- `dedupe(items: Iterable[F]) -> list[F]`: Keep the first fact per id, adding later evidence to it.
- `merge_screens(items: Iterable[Screen]) -> list[Screen]`: One screen per id. A Windows Forms form is written in two files (``MainForm.vb`` and ``MainForm.Designer.vb``): the code file names it, the designer file holds its controls.
- `merge_integrations(items: Iterable[Integration]) -> list[Integration]`
- `merge_npm_versions(items: Iterable[Library]) -> list[Library]`: A package that ``package.json`` declares and a lock file in the same folder pins is one library at the lock file's exact version, declared, with the ``package.json`` scope.
- `merge_libraries(items: Iterable[Library]) -> list[Library]`
- `techs_from_libraries(libs: Iterable[Library]) -> list[TechItem]`
- `merge_tech(items: Iterable[TechItem]) -> list[TechItem]`
- `merge_batch_jobs(items: Iterable[BatchJob]) -> list[BatchJob]`: The same job in several files (e.g. JIL exports): the later definition wins, evidence is kept from all of them.
- `merge_db_objects(items: Iterable[DbObject]) -> list[DbObject]`: Package spec and body are one object; definitions found twice keep all evidence.
- `group_by_service(items: list[Integration]) -> tuple[list[Integration], dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]`: All the usages of one external service as one row (decision 177): the endpoints of one host, the queues and channels of one queue manager, the files of one server or folder. The row lists what was grouped in ``endpoints``. Returns the rows, old id -> new id and old "TYPE target" label -> new label (services' external calls, web services' integrations).
- internal helpers: `_union`, `_evidence`, `_queue_direction`, `_consolidate`, `_merge_cft`, `_folder`, `_version_key`, `_qmgr_name`, `_service_key`, `_queue_managers`, `_endpoint`

### `legacy_audit.linker.link`

File: `legacy_audit/linker/link.py`

The linker: runs after every file has been analysed (or reloaded from the cache).

1. Merge per-file facts (integrations, libraries, tech, jobs, DB objects).
2. Resolve by-name references against symbols and file paths into ``CodeEdge``s; references
   that should resolve but do not become ``unresolved-reference`` findings.
3. Cross-link: screens reached from services (partials vs screens), SQL to tables (CRUD) and
   procedures, services to the tables and integrations they reach, batch jobs to services,
   COBOL sub-programs pruned from the service count, facts to components, component types.

Everything here is recomputed on every run, so new inputs (an Autosys export, a DDL dump) link
to source files whose analysis came from the cache.

- **class `LinkResult`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `entities`, `unresolved`, `edges`, `notes`, `warnings`
- `url_segments(url: str) -> list[str]`: Path segments of a route or of a URL built in code, parameters as ``{}``: ``/api/orders/:id`` and ``/api/orders/${id}`` (``/api/orders/?``) give ``['api', 'orders', '{}']``.
- `batch_scripts(entities: dict[str, list[Fact]], records: list[FileRecord]) -> dict[str, set[str]]`: Per component, the shell scripts that do batch work: they sit in a batch-like folder (batch, jobs, cron, ...), run SQL, or start a program, a Java class or a SQL file. A script that only calls other scripts, copies files or deploys is a utility, not batch work.
- `classify_components(components: list[Component], entities: dict[str, list[Fact]], records: list[FileRecord], fixed: set[str]) -> None`: Refine each component's type from what was found in it (overridden types are kept) and list every kind of work it holds in ``roles`` (decision 115). A component can be web *and* batch (a Struts module with its nightly ksh), batch with Java, ksh and properties, or only configuration.
- `link(records: list[FileRecord], facts: Iterable[Facts], copybook_paths: Iterable[str]=(), group_integrations: bool=True) -> LinkResult`
- internal class `_Index`
- internal class `_Linker` Methods: `__init__`, `comp`, `_pick`, `_path`, `_node_for_file`, `_node_for_symbol`, `_symbol`, `_source`, `_resolve`, `_api_route`, `_view`, `_edge`, `run`, `_step_failed`, `_mount_routes`, `_link_refs`, `_classify_screens`, `_prune_cobol`, `_hql_entities`, `_retarget_pruned`, `_link_sql`, `_node_files`, `_reach`, `_job_components`, `_owner_component`, `_components`
- internal helpers: `_build_index`, `_match_route`, `_file_id`, `_project_entries`, `_typed`, `_sorted`, `_dml_target`, `_crud`

### `legacy_audit.linker.maven`

File: `legacy_audit/linker/maven.py`

Maven versions a module inherits from its parent chain (``dependencyManagement`` and
properties), resolved once every ``pom.xml`` has been read.

- `resolve_versions(libraries: list[Library], symbols: list[Symbol]) -> list[Library]`
- internal helpers: `_substitute`

### `legacy_audit.linker.websvc`

File: `legacy_audit/linker/websvc.py`

One row per web service (decision 133).

**Offered** web services come from the ``Service`` facts that are web service operations
(``rest-operation``, ``soap-operation``, Node.js and NestJS routes, Spring handlers that return
data): operations of the same web service (``Service.web_service``, else the class or router
file) in one component are one row. Where the code is published (CXF ``jaxws:endpoint``,
``sun-jaxws.xml``, web.xml servlets) gives the row its address, and front-end or other code
calling a route is listed in ``callers``.

**Called** web services come from the client call sites the analyzers found and from the HTTP
and SOAP integrations (identity providers are login, not web services): one row per SOAP
endpoint address, per REST host, or per client name when the address is only known at run time.
A client whose name matches one with an address joins it.

**WSDL files** describe a service the application offers when an offered SOAP service has the
same name (``CustomerService``, ``CustomerServicePort``, ``CustomerServiceImpl`` are one name)
or most of its operations; else one it calls (same name or address); else, alone, a called
service when its address names another host, an offered one otherwise. A WSDL that describes
an offered service is not an outbound integration: its address is where the application is
called, so such integrations become inbound.

- `norm(name: str) -> str`: A web service name without the suffixes generated code adds: OrderService, OrderServicePort, OrderServiceSoapBindingStub and OrderServiceLocator are one name.
- `host_key(base: str) -> str`: ``host[:port]`` of a base URL without its scheme or default port: http and https calls to one host are one service.
- `build_web_services(raw: list[WebService], services: list[Service], integrations: list[Integration], symbols: list[Symbol], edges: list[CodeEdge], comp: Callable[[str | None], str | None], node_file: Callable[[str], str | None]) -> list[WebService]`
- internal class `_Builder` Methods: `__init__`, `build_offered`, `_key`, `_resolve`, `build_called`, `_called_row`, `_display`, `_pick_name`, `attach_contracts`, `finish`
- internal helpers: `_union`, `_ev`, `_add_ops`, `_common_path`, `_class_of`, `_stem`, `_group_name`, `_op_of`, `_plural`, `_describe`

## `legacy_audit.metrics`

### `legacy_audit.metrics`

File: `legacy_audit/metrics/__init__.py`

Metrics: code units, duplication, bands, dead code and effort.


### `legacy_audit.metrics.compute`

File: `legacy_audit/metrics/compute.py`

Cross-file metrics, recomputed every run from cached per-file results: duplication,
fan-in/fan-out, complexity scores and bands, dead-code candidates and per-component metrics.

Score of an item = sum over features of ``weight x feature / scale`` (``complexity`` in
``audit.yaml``). Features:

- services: ``loc`` and ``cyclomatic`` of the code the service runs (its handler, or its whole
  code file, plus code files reached within two hops over calls/uses/invokes/runs/triggers/
  includes edges), ``tables`` and ``integrations`` it reaches, ``vendor_sql`` (statements with
  vendor-specific features in that code) and ``fan_out``;
- screens: ``loc`` of the page, ``fields`` and ``fan_out``;
- batch jobs: the score of the job's ``batch-job`` service;
- components: the mean score of their services and screens.

- `band(score: float, thresholds: dict[str, float]) -> str`
- `score(features: dict[str, float], cfg: AuditConfig) -> float`
- **class `MetricsResult`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `metrics`, `units`, `dead_code`, `duplicated`, `features`
- `compute(cfg: AuditConfig, records: list[FileRecord], components: list[Component], entities: dict[str, list[Fact]], units: dict[str, list[CodeUnit]], windows: dict[str, list[list[int]]]) -> MetricsResult`: Fill complexity, scores and fan-in/out on services, screens and batch jobs (in place) and return per-component metrics plus the inputs of metric-based rules.
- internal class `_Graph` Methods: `__init__`, `reach`
- internal helpers: `_duplicated_lines`

### `legacy_audit.metrics.effort`

File: `legacy_audit/metrics/effort.py`

Effort model: person-days [low, likely, high] from the weights in ``effort.weights``.

Every item counted elsewhere is priced by its level: services, screens (not partials) and
batch jobs by complexity band; distinct SQL statements by PostgreSQL grade; stored code by
grade; integrations each; libraries by recommended action. The result is labelled
"estimate — weights from config": it is arithmetic on counts, not a forecast.

- `estimate(cfg: AuditConfig, entities: dict[str, list[Any]], component_of: dict[str, str | None]) -> EffortEstimate`: ``component_of`` maps a file path to its component (libraries list files).
- internal helpers: `_level`

### `legacy_audit.metrics.tokens`

File: `legacy_audit/metrics/tokens.py`

Comment stripping and token windows for duplication detection.

A window is ``window`` consecutive tokens starting at the first token of a line. Copy-pasted
blocks start at a line in both copies, so hashing one window per line finds them while storing
at most one hash per line in the file cache.

- `strip_comments(text: str, language: str) -> str`: Comments replaced by spaces; line breaks kept so line numbers stay valid.
- `windows(code: str, window: int) -> list[list[int]]`: ``[hash, first line, last line]`` for each window of ``window`` tokens that starts at the first token of a line.
- internal helpers: `_strip`, `_hash`

### `legacy_audit.metrics.units`

File: `legacy_audit/metrics/units.py`

Code units (functions, methods, paragraphs, procedures, scripts) and their cyclomatic
complexity: 1 + the number of decision points, counted per language.

- Java: ``if``, loops, ``case`` labels (not ``default``), ``catch``, ``?:``, ``&&``, ``||``.
- TypeScript/JavaScript: per function, method or arrow function (a short arrow function used
  as an argument, ``x => x.id``, is part of its enclosing unit): the same decision points as
  Java, plus ``??``.
- C/C++/Pro*C: the same, with ``case`` statements and range ``for``.
- C#: per method, constructor, operator, local function or property accessor with a body: the
  same as Java plus ``foreach``, ``??`` and switch-expression arms (not the ``_`` discard).
- VB6/VB.NET: per ``Sub``, ``Function``, ``Property`` or ``Operator``: ``If``/``ElseIf``,
  ``For``, ``While``/``Until`` (``Do``/``Loop`` conditions), ``Case`` (not ``Case Else``),
  ``Catch``, ``IIf(``/``If(``, ``AndAlso``/``OrElse``, and ``And``/``Or`` in a condition.
- COBOL: per paragraph or section: ``IF``, ``WHEN`` (not ``WHEN OTHER``), ``UNTIL``, ``AND``,
  ``OR``, and the conditional phrases ``AT END``, ``INVALID KEY``, ``ON SIZE ERROR``,
  ``ON EXCEPTION``, ``ON OVERFLOW``.
- PL/SQL: per procedure, function, trigger or package body: ``IF``, ``ELSIF``, ``WHEN``,
  ``LOOP``/``WHILE``/``FOR`` loops.
- Shell and other scripts: one unit per file: ``if``, ``elif``, loops, ``case`` branches,
  ``&&``, ``||``.

- `ts_units(code: str, path: str) -> list[CodeUnit]`: Units of TypeScript or JavaScript code: named functions, methods, and arrow functions or function expressions that are assigned or are multi-line callbacks.
- `tree_units(code: str, language: str) -> list[CodeUnit]`: Units of Java or C/C++ code (Pro*C callers pass the text with EXEC SQL blanked).
- `cs_units(code: str) -> list[CodeUnit]`: Units of C# code; an accessor without a body (``get;``) is not one.
- `vb_units(code: str) -> list[CodeUnit]`: Procedures of VB6 or VB.NET code (``Declare`` and abstract members have no body).
- `cobol_units(code_lines: list[str]) -> list[CodeUnit]`: Paragraphs and sections of the PROCEDURE DIVISION (``code_lines`` from ``cobol.source_lines``: code area only, comments blanked).
- `plsql_units(code: str) -> list[CodeUnit]`: Procedures, functions, triggers and package bodies; inside a package body each procedure/function is its own unit. Plain SQL scripts have none.
- `script_unit(code: str, language: str, name: str) -> list[CodeUnit]`
- internal helpers: `_parser`, `_nonblank`, `_is_logical`, `_decisions`, `_walk`, `_name`, `_ts_name`, `_ts_decisions`, `_cs_name`, `_cs_decisions`

## `legacy_audit.report`

### `legacy_audit.report`

File: `legacy_audit/report/__init__.py`

Report generators (phase 4: technical HTML site).


### `legacy_audit.report.batches`

File: `legacy_audit/report/batches.py`

One consolidated batch list: every batch with a short description and when it runs.

A batch is a batch flow (``flows.batch_flows``): a scheduled box or job, or, when no scheduler
definition covers it, a batch component, a program or a listener. Each row says what the batch
does and when it runs, and where each of the two came from:

- *what it does*: the Copilot story's purpose (stage 12, labelled AI), else the scheduler's own
  description, else the first line of the code's header comment, else the scan's sentence;
- *when it runs*: the scheduler definition (JIL, JCL, crontab, Spring Batch), else the AI story's
  ``when``, else a hint read from the code (``@Scheduled`` or Quartz cron expressions, comments
  such as "nightly" or "runs at 02:00"), else "no schedule found" with the inputs that are
  missing.

Hints are copied from the source with their file and line, never guessed (rule 1); they are
read at report time from the scanned source, like the header comments (decision 103).

- `schedule_hint(rd: RunData, f: Flow) -> dict[str, Any] | None`: The first schedule the code of a batch states: its own files first, then the rest of its component (configuration holds Quartz triggers). ``{text, file, line}`` or None.
- `batch_list(rd: RunData, batch_flows: list[Flow], said: dict[str, str], stories: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`: One row per batch, scheduled or not, in name order.
- internal helpers: `_cron_text`, `_hint_in_text`, `_what_it_runs`, `_missing_inputs`

### `legacy_audit.report.catalogues`

File: `legacy_audit/report/catalogues.py`

Catalogue tables: which columns each entity shows, and its rows as plain lists.

A catalogue is written next to the pages as ``data/<name>.js`` (``LA_DATA["<name>"] = {...}``)
and drawn by ``report.js`` with search, per-column filters, sorting and paging. A script file and
not JSON, because browsers refuse ``fetch()`` on pages opened from disk (``file://``).

Column types: ``text``, ``num``, ``code`` (monospace), ``badge`` (grade/severity chip),
``list`` (comma-joined), ``link`` (``{text, href}`` to another report page) and ``evidence``
(``{text, href, vscode}`` to the source file). ``filter: true`` adds a value filter above the
column.

- **class `Column`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `key`, `label`, `type`, `filter`
  - `spec() -> dict[str, Any]`
- **class `Catalogue`** `@dataclass`
  - fields: `name`, `title`, `intro`, `columns`, `rows`
  - `payload() -> dict[str, Any]`
  - `drop(key: str) -> None`: Remove a column (and its cell in every row), e.g. the PostgreSQL grade when there is no target.
- `ws_text(ws: dict[str, Any], story: dict[str, Any] | None) -> tuple[str, str]`: (what it is for, suggested migration): the Copilot story (stage 12) marked AI, else the scan's sentence and nothing.
- `ws_label(ws: dict[str, Any]) -> str`
- `build(rd: RunData, root: Path, stories: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None=None, ws_stories: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None=None) -> dict[str, Catalogue]`: Every catalogue of the run; ``root`` is the report folder (evidence links are relative). ``stories`` are the Copilot interface stories by integration id and ``ws_stories`` its web service stories by web service id, when the stage exists.
- `batches(rd: RunData, root: Path, rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> Catalogue`: The consolidated batch list (``report/batches.py``): one row per batch, scheduled or not, with what it does and when it runs, and where each came from.
- internal helpers: `_comp`, `_ev`, `_join`, `_library_name`, `_ai_or`, `_recommended`, `_crud_matrix`

### `legacy_audit.report.comments`

File: `legacy_audit/report/comments.py`

What a program says about itself: the header comment of a source file.

Batch programs usually open with a comment saying what they do ("Nightly settlement: load,
extract, send to the bank"). The functional document shows that text beside the scan's flow, so
a reader learns what a batch is for even before the Copilot agent has written anything. The text
is copied, never interpreted; credentials in it are masked like everywhere else.

- `mask_secrets(text: str) -> str`: Hide passwords, tokens and user/password@db credentials in a line of source.

What a report reads: one run folder (``run.json``, ``data/*.json``, ``logs/``), plus where the
